findings.claim: Logic is better represented as a cross-domain foundational/methodological axis than as an ordinary child of mathematics.
Computation and information require distinct but overlapping identities; neither should be collapsed into software engineering or communications.
Astronomy deserves first-class major-domain representation, while cosmology is currently better modeled as a physics↔astronomy major bridge/subspace.
Earth science/geoscience deserves first-class major-domain representation; atmosphere, ocean and geology are major subspaces, while climate is a cross-system bridge.
Cognitive science is an interdisciplinary bridge-domain discipline, not a subclass of psychology; neuroscience and linguistics also require first-class identities with multi-domain placement.
Measurement/metrology is a cross-domain methodological/epistemic axis and must not be forced under a single object-domain.

next: Round2B should normalize Physical/Material, Life, Engineering/Intervention, Historical/Symbolic and biomedical/agricultural boundary candidates.

normalizedSpaces.label: Logic
normalizedSpaces.rationale: MSC treats mathematical logic and foundations as a major mathematical class whose internal structure includes philosophical logic, general logic, computability, set theory and proof theory. This supports one logic identity spanning multiple domains rather than a mathematics-only child.

normalizedSpaces.label: Computation and computing
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Computability appears inside mathematical logic while ACM maintains a broad taxonomy for the computing field; computation therefore crosses formal theory and technological realization.

normalizedSpaces.label: Information theory
normalizedSpaces.rationale: IEEE defines information theory around mathematical underpinnings of information processing, transmission, storage and use, with coding, complexity, cryptography, learning and stochastic processes. It is broader than a communications-engineering subfield but not yet justified as a standalone root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Astronomy and astrophysics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: IAU organizes astronomy through nine divisions ranging from Fundamental Astronomy through planetary, stellar, interstellar, high-energy and galaxies/cosmology, demonstrating a first-class domain topology that should not be collapsed to one physics subnode.

normalizedSpaces.label: Cosmology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: IAU places Galaxies and Cosmology within a dedicated division while high-energy/fundamental physics is separately represented; cosmology is therefore best treated as a major cross-boundary subspace, not a root by default.

normalizedSpaces.label: Earth science / geoscience
normalizedSpaces.rationale: AGU explicitly spans Earth and space sciences and maintains many sections across atmosphere, biogeosciences, cryosphere, surface processes, geodesy and geomagnetism, supporting a first-class geoscience system domain.

normalizedSpaces.label: Geology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Geology is substantial but current evidence is consistent with major subspace status inside a broader geoscience/Earth-system region.

normalizedSpaces.label: Geophysics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: AGU section structure exposes multiple explicitly physical Earth domains, supporting a physics↔Earth bridge identity rather than exclusive parentage.

normalizedSpaces.label: Atmospheric science and meteorology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Atmospheric Sciences is an explicit AGU section and participates in broader Earth-system interactions; treat as major subspace with system-domain character.

normalizedSpaces.label: Oceanography
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Ocean science is inherently physical, chemical, biological and Earth-systemic; exclusive placement under one natural science would lose its topology.

normalizedSpaces.label: Climate science
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Climate cuts across atmospheric, oceanic, cryospheric, biogeochemical and surface-process regions and should be represented as a system bridge rather than a single-parent branch.

normalizedSpaces.label: Cognitive science
normalizedSpaces.rationale: The Cognitive Science Society explicitly promotes cognitive science as a discipline and names AI, linguistics, anthropology, psychology, neuroscience, philosophy and education as contributing areas. It must not be modeled as a psychology subclass.

normalizedSpaces.label: Psychology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Psychology contains cognition-focused empirical science but also extends beyond cognition; current evidence supports an independent major domain identity, not reduction to cognitive science or social science.

normalizedSpaces.label: Neuroscience
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Neuroscience connects biological mechanisms, medical contexts and cognitive/psychological phenomena; preserve bridge status rather than force a single parent.

normalizedSpaces.label: Linguistics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: LSA describes its mission as advancing the scientific study of language and publishes across semantics, pragmatics, phonology, syntax and related interfaces; cognitive science independently treats linguistics as a contributing field. Linguistics therefore warrants first-class identity with multiple bridges.

normalizedSpaces.label: Measurement and metrology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: VIM defines metrology as the science of measurement and its application, including all theoretical and practical aspects regardless of uncertainty or field. This is a cross-domain methodological axis, not an ordinary physics or engineering child.

policies.identityVsRole: Identity normalization and role classification are separate.
policies.multiRole: A space may have multiple roleClasses and placements.
policies.rootAdmission: All Round2A spaces remain NOT_ADMITTED as canonical roots.
policies.sourceAuthority: Professional/domain classification structures inform topology but do not mint Ordivon ontology truth.
